message.content:
I bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90 (filled at $222.90, ~$9,808 total), which is within the $10,000 per-order cap and leaves the $20,000 daily budget with room for a possible MSFT order; no funds were moved out of the account.

**Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent results — the fiscal Q4 2024 report released October 31, 2024 (quarter ended September 28, 2024) — which showed quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion, up 6% year over year, and full-year fiscal 2024 net sales of $391.0 billion (vs. $383.3 billion in FY2023), net income of $93.7 billion, operating income of $123.2 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.08 (down from $6.13, reflecting a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge). News flow on the day was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual rollout of Apple Intelligence, with no negative catalyst in the coverage I found. Given steady top-line growth, very high margins and profitability, a modest valuation (~36x trailing EPS) and a quote of $222.70 last / $222.72 ask, I judged a small starter position appropriate rather than a large commitment, so I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $222.90 — essentially at market — which filled at $222.90 for about $9,808, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily limits and leaving my $50,000 cash balance largely intact.

Actually a limit buy fills at the limit or better; filling at exactly the limit when ask was 222.72 is a minor slippage artifact. Not a big deal, but worth noting. Total $9,807.60, under $10,000.
